name: cc65
why: A C compiler targeting the 6502 processor, a real retro toolchain for running code on vintage hardware.

brief.what_it_is: cc65 is a cross-development suite for 6502-family (65(C)02) systems. It bundles a C compiler (cc65) with a macro assembler (ca65), linker (ld65), archiver (ar65), object-file tools (co65, od65, da65), a simulator (sim65), and other utilities such as chrcvt65, grc65, sp65 and cl65. You feed it C or assembly source and it produces machine code and binaries for old 6502 machines. It ships C and runtime library support for many of those machines.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a complete cross-development package for 65(C)02 systems, giving developers a real C toolchain for vintage hardware. It is originally based on Ron Cain's Small C compiler, enhanced by James E. Hendrix, and was later moved to modern systems and largely rewritten by Ullrich von Bassewitz.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internal mechanism. It says the package has a compiler, assembler, linker, archiver and simulator, and that a generic configuration exists for adapting it to new targets. Target machines are supported through per-machine libraries and configuration.
brief.install_notes: Homebrew's caveat says library files are installed to $HOMEBREW_CELLAR/cc65/2.19/share/cc65, so the runtime libraries live in that share directory. The README lists Windows 64-bit and 32-bit snapshot zips on SourceForge and a Linux snapshot DEB/RPM via openSUSE Build Service. No accounts or extra runtimes are mentioned. Target machines like the C64 or NES need their own emulator or hardware to run output.
brief.standout: It is a full retro toolchain rather than a single compiler, covering many 8-bit machines from Apple II and Atari to NES, C64, PC Engine and Commander X16 in one package. The target table in the README is long and specific, and the project still has active targets such as the RP6502 Picocomputer.
brief.status: Probably maintained, though the evidence is indirect. The Homebrew formula is at version 2.19. The README has a live GitHub Actions snapshot-build badge on master, a named core team, and an active discussions board and IRC channel. I did not see a release date or last-commit date, so this is not confirmed.
brief.caveats: The homepage fetch returned almost no content (only a title and a host name), so most of this brief comes from the GitHub README. Output is for retro hardware, so you need an emulator or real machine to run it. The README links Windows and Linux snapshots rather than tagged releases in the text I read, and the Windows zips point to SourceForge. Some target support is marked as contributed by individuals and may vary in completeness. The README says its team list is incomplete.
quotes: cc65 is a complete cross-development package for 65(C)02 systems, including a powerful macro assembler, a C compiler, linker, archiver, simulator and several other tools.
cc65 has C and runtime library support for many of the old 6502 machines.
A generic configuration to adapt cc65 to new targets is also around.
